context: The agent was asked to triage two independent PR review comments. Scenario 1: missing resource limits on a Kubernetes container, which it must classify, produce corrected YAML for, and write a review reply to. Scenario 2: a comment names a function that was renamed before the pinned PR head, where the underlying bug persists under the new name; the agent must investigate the rename rather than treat the absent identifier as evidence the bug is already fixed.

checklist.name: correct_classification
checklist.description: Classifies the comment as ACTIONABLE_FIX — missing resource limits is a real safety issue that must be fixed

checklist.name: correct_yaml
checklist.description: Provides corrected YAML with resources.requests (cpu + memory) and resources.limits (memory). CPU limit is omitted or justified — CPU limits cause throttling.

checklist.name: blast_radius
checklist.description: States blast radius: rolling update replaces pods; if requests exceed actual usage, pods may be rescheduled

checklist.name: rollback_plan
checklist.description: Provides a rollback plan: revert manifest and re-apply, or kubectl rollout undo

checklist.name: reply_quality
checklist.description: Review reply is concise and references the specific file (`apps/api/deployment.yaml`) and/or the specific change made (resource requests/limits added)

checklist.name: no_absence_as_fixed
checklist.description: Does not classify as `ALREADY_FIXED` or `NOT_APPLICABLE` merely because the original identifier is absent; investigates the renamed target and confirms the bug status there.

checklist.name: execution_state_separate_from_classification
checklist.description: States fix/publish/resolution status as a distinct field from the classification, not conflated into one verdict.
